report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Run node ids with solo fallback, validate task schema, manage disposable worktrees, apply test overlay/reference patch, and define Selection dataclass.

symbols.name: run_node_ids
symbols.note: Runs pytest batch then solo re-runs for unattributed nodes; refuses primary checkout.

symbols.name: TestRunner
symbols.note: Type alias for injectable test runner callable.

symbols.name: REQUIRED_FIELDS
symbols.note: Tuple of required task fields: id, repo, base_revision, fail_to_pass.

symbols.name: validate_task
symbols.note: Returns list of schema problems; never raises.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task.

symbols.name: disposable_worktree
symbols.note: Context manager creating a git worktree via GitWorktreeManager, yields path, cleans up.

symbols.name: apply_test_overlay
symbols.note: Writes test files from test_revision into worktree using git show.

symbols.name: reference_patch
symbols.note: Returns git diff base..reference as bytes, excluding given paths.

symbols.name: apply_patch
symbols.note: Applies patch with git apply; returns None or error reason.

symbols.name: Selection
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding measured selection; includes digest method (defined elsewhere).

claims.text: Run exactly these node ids inside worktree and attribute per node.
claims.why: The function deduplicates node ids, runs them in a batch, then solo re-runs unattributed ones, attributing statuses per node via parse_pytest_output.

claims.text: Batch first (one interpreter start, ~2.2s on this box, measured), then RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed.
claims.why: The code runs _spawn_pytest with all nodes, then loops over unattributed nodes and spawns solo pytest for each.

claims.text: That fallback is not belt-and-braces, it is required: measured on this box, a single node id pytest cannot collect aborts the WHOLE invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs -- even with --continue-on-collection-errors.
claims.why: The claim about pytest behavior and exit codes is external; this chunk does not contain the measurement or pytest internals, but the code's solo re-run logic is consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Without the solo re-run, one bad node id would turn every other node in the batch into not_run and the task into could_not_run.
claims.why: The causal chain depends on pytest's behavior and downstream task classification, which are not fully visible in this chunk.

claims.text: worktree is refused if it is the primary checkout or inside it.
claims.why: The function calls _refuse_primary_checkout(worktree, repo_root, "pytest working directory") at the start.

claims.text: Every schema problem with task, or []. Never raises.
claims.why: The function returns a list of problems and does not raise; it handles non-dict input and checks each field with .get().

claims.text: An EMPTY fail_to_pass is an error, not an empty success: a task with no test that must go from red to green cannot fail, and a measurement that cannot fail is the exact defect harness._recall's vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: The code checks `if not task.get(key)` for REQUIRED_FIELDS, which includes fail_to_pass, so an empty or missing fail_to_pass produces a problem.

claims.text: True for a task carrying the correctness format. Mirrored in daedalus.eval.tasks so the harness can refuse to grade one with substring recall; defined there, re-exported here for callers who already have this module imported.
claims.why: The function delegates to .tasks.is_correctness_task; the implementation and the mirroring in tasks module are not in this chunk.

claims.text: A checkout of revision that is NOT the primary checkout.
claims.why: It uses GitWorktreeManager.create_worktree and then _refuse_primary_checkout on the resulting path.

claims.text: Delegates to daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager on purpose rather than shelling out to git worktree add: that class places worktrees outside the checkout, refuses an allocation whose path is repo-adjacent, and owns a recursive delete that re-verifies every component before every syscall.
claims.why: The behavior of GitWorktreeManager is not in this chunk; only its use is visible.

claims.text: Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no shutil.rmtree here and there must never be one.
claims.why: In this chunk, the only deletion is via manager.cleanup_worktree; no shutil.rmtree appears.

claims.text: The branch ref that git worktree add -b writes into the shared .git is reaped afterwards through the manager's own reap_branches, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.
claims.why: The reap_branches implementation and its guarantees are in GitWorktreeManager, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Write the task's test files, as of test_revision, into the worktree.
claims.why: The function iterates paths, uses _git_read to get blob content at test_revision, and writes bytes to target.

claims.text: This is SWE-bench's "test patch", and it is what makes a before-state measurable at all: the base revision predates the fix, so it also predates the fix's tests -- running a FAIL_TO_PASS node against a bare base checkout would only ever report missing.
claims.why: The claim about SWE-bench and before-state measurability involves broader context not in this chunk, though the code does write test files.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (git show <rev>:<path>), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
claims.why: The code uses _git_read to obtain proc.stdout bytes and writes them directly with target.write_bytes(proc.stdout).

claims.text: Raises FileNotFoundError if a path does not exist at that revision, and OverlayEscape if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: It raises FileNotFoundError when proc.returncode != 0; _safe_join is expected to raise OverlayEscape (defined elsewhere) for escape paths.

claims.text: The known-good change as a patch: git diff base..reference.
claims.why: The function constructs git diff arguments and calls _git_read.

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the "after" run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: The function appends :(exclude) pathspecs for each rel in exclude.

claims.text: Apply patch_bytes inside the worktree. Returns None, or the reason.
claims.why: The function returns None on success and a string describing failure on git apply refusal.

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a could_not_run, never a not_fixed: "the change was rejected by git" and "the change did not fix the bug" are different facts about different things.
claims.why: The mapping to could_not_run vs not_fixed is determined by the caller/state machine, not in this chunk.

claims.text: WHAT WILL BE MEASURED, fixed before any candidate code runs.
claims.why: The dataclass is frozen and contains all measurement parameters.

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so "what was measured is what was declared" is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring.
claims.why: The class is decorated with @dataclass(frozen=True) and fields fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, test_overlay are tuples.

claims.text: Everything a result depends on is in here: both node id lists, the RESOLVED base sha (not the ref that was typed), the overlay revision and paths, and the gate configuration.
claims.why: The fields include base_revision, fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, test_revision, test_overlay, gate, timeout_s; but the claim that base_revision is RESOLVED is not verifiable here; it depends on how Selection is constructed elsewhere.

claims.text: digest covers all of it. Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes, which is what lets correctness_gate refuse a task that was verified under one selection and presented under another.
claims.why: The digest property is not defined in this chunk; only referenced in to_dict.

observations.what: run_node_ids: when timed_out from batch, returns immediately without solo re-runs for unattributed nodes; solo re-runs only happen if not timed_out. This may leave unattributed nodes as not_run despite the docstring's promise to re-run every unattributed node.

run_node_ids: if len(unattributed) == len(nodes) == 1, it returns without solo re-run, contradicting the docstring's 'RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed' (though the docstring's rationale about aborting whole invocation doesn't apply when there's only one node).

run_node_ids: containment is updated as solo_containment if containment == 'none' else containment; if batch containment is 'none' and solo containment is 'none', it stays 'none'; if batch containment is e.g. 'partial', solo containment is ignored, which may misreport containment.

validate_task: checks REQUIRED_FIELDS with `if not task.get(key)`, so an empty string for 'repo' or 'base_revision' is treated as missing; for 'id' an empty string is also missing; this is fine but the error message says 'missing or empty required field' which matches.

validate_task: for 'fail_to_pass' and 'pass_to_pass', it checks each entry for '::' but not for 'test_overlay' entries; the docstring says 'test_overlay' entries should be file paths, not node ids, so that's consistent.

disposable_worktree: if keep=True, the worktree is not cleaned up and reap_branches is not called; the docstring says cleanup is the only delete, but with keep=True no cleanup happens, which may be intentional but the docstring doesn't mention it.
apply_test_overlay: uses _safe_join to prevent escape, but if _safe_join raises OverlayEscape, it propagates; the docstring says it raises OverlayEscape, so that's kept.
apply_patch: uses tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with delete=False and then os.unlink in finally; if os.unlink fails, the exception is swallowed, potentially leaving a temp file.

apply_patch: the patch is applied with `git apply --whitespace=nowarn`, but the docstring doesn't mention whitespace handling; the return reason string is truncated to 800 chars, which may lose information.

Selection.to_dict: includes 'argv_shape' computed from pytest_node_argv(('<node>',)) which is a constant shape, but the digest is computed elsewhere; the docstring says digest covers all, but digest is not visible here.

risks: run_node_ids | high | On batch timeout, solo re-runs are skipped, leaving unattributed nodes as not_run; docstring promises re-run for every unattributed node; would be settled by checking the code path when timed_out is True and unattributed is non-empty.

run_node_ids | medium | Single unattributed node returns without solo re-run despite docstring's general promise; likely intentional but undocumented; would be settled by reading the docstring's next sentence about aborting whole invocation.
run_node_ids | low | Containment aggregation may ignore solo containment when batch containment is not 'none'; would be settled by checking how containment is used downstream.
disposable_worktree | low | keep=True skips cleanup and branch reaping; docstring doesn't mention this; would be settled by reading the context manager's caller expectations.
apply_patch | low | Temp file unlink failure is swallowed; could leak files; would be settled by checking if os.unlink failure is acceptable.
Selection | low | to_dict includes argv_shape but not the full argv; digest is not in chunk; would be settled by reading the digest property definition.
validate_task | low | Empty string for 'repo' or 'base_revision' is treated as missing, but a revision of '' is invalid anyway; would be settled by checking task creation code.
apply_test_overlay | low | OverlayEscape is raised by _safe_join, but the docstring says it raises it; no issue.
reference_patch | low | The exclude pathspecs are appended after '--' and '.', which might not work as expected with git diff; would be settled by testing git diff with exclude pathspecs.
apply_patch | low | The error message is truncated to 800 chars, which might hide the full git apply error; would be settled by checking if truncation is intentional.
